I like owning the whole path: architecture, development, testing and the release to App Store and Google Play. I care about apps that stay fast and stable as they grow, and I once made a large Hajj app 65% smaller by rebuilding its structure.

Outside my day job I co-founded two products. I lead the tech team at Adrenaline Platform, and I'm the only mobile developer behind Dikirnis On, a local super-app that reached 2,500+ users in its first five months.

seo.title: Dikirnis On case study: a local super-app in Flutter | Atef Elsaeed
seo.description: How I built Dikirnis On alone: a Flutter super-app with 10+ sectors, 2,500+ users and 500+ businesses in 5 months, using one data-driven listing UI.

cases.title: Dikirnis On

summary.dd: A local super-app for Dikirnis, Egypt. One place for 10+ sectors: doctors and clinic bookings, jobs, a buy-and-sell market, stores and offers, home and car services, education, sports, restaurant ordering and local news. A second app, Dikirnis On Pro, lets businesses run their own store.
2,500+ users and 500+ registered businesses within 5 months of the May 2026 launch.

more.dd: Co-founder and the only mobile developer. I built both apps with Flutter, Bloc and go_router, integrated with a .NET REST API, and handle every store release.

Most sectors are listings, so I built one data-driven listing UI instead of a screen per sector. Categories nest to any depth. When the team adds or reorders a sector in the dashboard, it appears in the app right away, with no new release. Features with their own logic (jobs, the market, bookings) are separate modules.

seo.title: Prime Source case study: Hajj app cut from 250 to 85 MB | Atef Elsaeed
seo.description: A Hajj operations app for five user roles had grown to 250 MB. Re-architecting it and removing duplicate assets and dead code made the download 65% smaller.

summary.dd: An operations app for organizing Hajj: pilgrim housing, transport and on-site coordination, plus Quran, Athkar and Duas. Five kinds of users share one app, each with their own job.
From 250 MB to 85 MB, a 65% smaller download for pilgrims who often install it on mobile data.

more.dd: The app had grown to 250 MB. It carried many font files, duplicated images and assets, a lot of dead code, unused packages, and an architecture that made every change harder.
Re-structured the whole app, removed duplicate fonts and images, dead code and unused dependencies, then shipped a redesign with new features and performance improvements.

seo.title: RepoSphere case study: one inbox for all your Git work | Atef Elsaeed
seo.description: RepoSphere is an open-source Flutter dashboard for GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps and Gitea. Clean Architecture, Riverpod, one repository per provider, CI on every push.

cases.tag: Open source · live demo · in active development
cases.title: RepoSphere

summary.dd: A unified dashboard for developers who work across many repositories on more than one Git provider. Repos, commits, pull requests, issues, releases, notifications and gists from GitHub, GitLab, Azure DevOps and Gitea in one place, instead of switching between tabs and accounts.

Clean Architecture with domain, data and presentation layers, Riverpod for state and GoRouter for navigation. Each provider has its own data source behind one repository, so GitLab was added without touching the screens. GitHub sign-in uses the OAuth Device Flow, tokens live in secure storage, and an expired token anywhere in the app logs the user out through one global observer.

more.dd: Built solo and open source, from the product spec and design system to the code. Flutter, web-first, with the same codebase targeting Android, iOS, macOS, Windows and Linux.
GitHub Actions runs static analysis, tests and a web build on every push. Sentry for crash reporting. Work is planned in sprints and documented in the repository.
Multi-account support, so one person can connect several GitHub and GitLab accounts, for example one per client.

seo.title: Belmally ERP case study: four apps on one API | Atef Elsaeed
seo.description: Belmally is a multi-tenant ERP I am building alone: a NestJS API, a React dashboard, a Flutter desktop POS and a Flutter field-sales app, with double-entry accounting and per-customer modules.

cases.title: Belmally ERP

summary.dd: A multi-tenant ERP for distribution, retail and light manufacturing businesses. One core (inventory, sales, double-entry accounting, purchasing, expenses, reports) with industry modules that are switched on per customer: manufacturing, device and warranty tracking, installments, maintenance, approvals, CRM and multi-branch.
In development, with no customers yet. Built alone since May 2026: 45 API controllers, 82 database entities and four apps that share one API.

more.dd: Founder and the only developer: product scope, database and API design, the accounting engine, all four apps, the Docker setup and the CI/CD pipeline.

Every financial action posts its own double-entry journal lines, so the books can't drift away from sales, purchases, expenses and returns. Stock is an append-only ledger. Every table carries a tenant id taken from the login token. Document numbers are issued under a database lock, so two cashiers never get the same invoice number. Modules are feature flags per customer, so one code base can serve a supermarket and a repair shop. Arabic is the default language, with English and right-to-left layouts on all four apps.

One shared API contract file is checked by the backend, the web app, the desktop app and the mobile app, so the API and its clients can't drift apart. About 520 automated tests across the four apps, end-to-end scripts that run against a real server and database, and a CI pipeline that also checks that the migrations build the same schema as the entities.
Still open: Egyptian e-invoicing (ETA), which waits for a real customer; push-notification setup; and testing receipt printing and camera barcode scanning on real devices.

seo.title: XPrinter App case study: PDFs on Bluetooth thermal printers | Atef Elsaeed
seo.description: An Android app that prints PDF files on 80 mm Bluetooth thermal printers: each page is rendered to an image at the printer's resolution and sent as ESC/POS commands over a native Bluetooth socket.

cases.title: XPrinter App

summary.dd: An Android app that prints PDF files on 80 mm Bluetooth thermal printers. The user picks a paired printer, chooses a PDF on the device or opens one from another app (Open with, or Share), and prints.

more.dd: Built on my own, from the Flutter app to the native Android Bluetooth code.

Thermal printers don't understand PDFs. The app renders each page to an image at the printer's resolution (203 DPI, 576 dots across for 80 mm), turns it grayscale and sends it as ESC/POS image commands, so any PDF prints the way it looks on screen, with no fonts or code pages to handle per printer. The Bluetooth plugin only lists paired devices, so a small Kotlin channel opens the Bluetooth SPP socket and sends the bytes.
Feature-first Clean Architecture with Riverpod and go_router.
